cars.specification_market: Second-generation BD/BG Legacy / Liberty sporting-road family, selected 1996 Japan Touring Wagon GT-B automatic as catalogued in Subaru's retrospective museum library. One family across sedan/wagon, GT/GT-B/RS grades, Limited, regional names, engines, transmissions, years and related Outback/Lancaster versions. Existing BC/BF, BE/BH and BL/BP entries are other generations. Selected automatic has 260 PS and E-4AT, not the manual's 280 PS. EJ20 only: no suffix, direct injection, compression, mass, detailed centre-control ratio or record-run speed inferred. The generic DIT footer on the museum page does not describe this engine. Museum catalogue reference is not claimed to be an individually inspected period brochure.
cars.summary: The second-generation Legacy GT-B helped define Japan's high-performance sporting-wagon boom, combining two-stage twin-turbo boxer power, all-wheel drive and Bilstein inverted dampers with family-wagon practicality. Manufacturer history and a retrospective driving report support its cultural and engineering significance; the report also records the limitations of its aged test car. Count the entire second-generation sporting-road family once.

sources.title: BOXER 60th Anniversary engineer interview — 1996 GT-B engine development
sources.notes: Introduction and relevant GT-B development section read, not an entire multi-part interview audit. Explicitly separates June 1996 280 PS five-speed manual and 260 PS E-four-speed automatic. Everyday usability and sporting-wagon intent provide context. EJ20R injector discussion concerns the manual project and supplies no selected automatic engine suffix or injector specification.

sources.title: Subaru Legacy cumulative production reaches three million — 15 March 2005 chronology
sources.notes: Relevant release body and chronology read. Records second-generation launch in October 1993, GT wagon role in Japan's emerging station-wagon market, and June 1996 GT-B with Bilstein inverted dampers. Generic 280 PS chronology entry is not assigned to the selected automatic. FIA speed-record figures, first-generation rally results and later-generation records are not production GT-B specifications.

sources.title: Review: Subaru Legacy in Retrospect, Vol.2 — 今尾直樹, 16 October 2019
sources.source_type: Original retrospective road drive and reporting
sources.notes: Introduction and second-generation GT-B driving section read through AWD discussion and its context. Author drove a 1997 first-registered automatic, not the selected 1996 catalogue reference. Reports Japanese wagon-boom popularity and confident wet-road/cornering character, alongside noise, heavy steering and aged test-car body, ride and braking limitations. No numerical specification imported; conflicting 1460/1470 kg figures are omitted. Earlier-generation rally wins are not attributed to GT-B.
